newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat after deals reprice.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat after deals reprice.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds finished Tuesday mostly unchanged with the focus on supply and repricings for the day's large new issues.
PaineWebber Inc. said it repriced $599 million San Antonio, Texas, electric system bonds, lowering yields in several maturities but leaving the top yield in 2020 unchanged at 5.75 percent.
Dillon, Read & Co. said it restructured New York State Thruway Authority's $350 million bond deal, adjusting the coupon in 2027 but leaving the top yield in 2027 unchanged at 5.75 percent.
In competitive action, Lehman Brothers won the day's largest competitive deal, a $53 million Hamilton County, Tenn., general obligation issue.
Lehman reoffered the 2009 maturity at a 5.20 percent yield, and did not formally reoffer the 2010 through 2012 maturities.
Muni sales for Wednesday are expected to total $1.6 billion in 28 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings total $1.2 billion in 11 sales, with a $450 million Puerto Rico Electric Power deal through Bear, Stearns & Co., Inc. topping the list.
On the competitive side, 17 sales totaling $418 million are on the schedule. A $173 million Tennessee deal at 1030 EDT is the largest.
The Treasury market was slightly weaker, amid disappointment over demand for Tuesday's auction of $17 billion of three-year notes.
Following the auction, the government long bond was down 5/32 at 96-21/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
Another $12 billion of 10-year notes are set for auction Wednesday.
In debt futures, June municipal bonds closed 5/32 higher at 115-9/32, while June Treasury bonds rose 2/32 to 110-3/32. The MOB spread widened to 166 ticks from 163 at the close on Monday.
In the secondary market, bids on Delaware River Port Authority FGIC 5-1/2s of 2026 rose one basis point to 5.75 percent.
Port Authority of New York and New Jersey JFK International Air Terminal MBIA 5.75s of 2022 fell two basis points to 5.92 percent, after being quoted unchanged at midday.
